validation.title: Validation
validation.notLoadedDesc: Place the observed Sentinel-1 flood mask and the ARGUS modelled flood in {path} (observed.tif|geojson, modelled.tif|geojson). Metrics are computed only from supplied data.
validation.syntheticWarning: SYNTHETIC SELF-TEST — verifies the metric pipeline only. It is not evidence of model skill.
validation.formula: IoU = TP/(TP+FP+FN) · Precision = TP/(TP+FP) · Recall = TP/(TP+FN)
validation.holdoutNot: Not independent future-event forecast accuracy · not hydrodynamic validation · not certified government accuracy.
validation.rowDirect: Direct mask comparison over the whole satellite AOI (native grid)
validation.protocolText: Recomputed by ARGUS from observed.tif / modelled.tif on the {grid} m DEM grid; alternating {block} m blocks; excluded: pixels unusable in either optical scene, slope > {slope}°, > {dist} km from the river, JRC water occurrence ≥ {jrc}%.
validation.directExplain: The direct comparison also counts permanent water and terrain far from the river, which the documented protocol excludes — hence the lower score.
validation.noS1: Sentinel-1: no suitable acquisition for the event window — not fabricated.
validation.noXY: terrain/hydro features only, no raw X/Y coordinates
validation.qcFigure: QC figure from the data pack: flood-period vs post-recession spectral comparison and extracted mask

methodology.title: Methodology and limitations

stress.robustness: Robustness = feasible scenarios ÷ evaluated scenarios. A scenario is feasible when no task is infeasible; at-risk tasks are reported but counted as feasible.
stress.perturbations: Perturbations: next higher forecast members; flood peak 60/120 min earlier; each road on the plan's routes closing 60 min earlier; most-used roads unavailable; each assigned crew 30 min late; each assigned vehicle and one pump per pump task unavailable; two combined cases.
stress.limitations: Perturbations are single-factor or pairwise, not a probabilistic ensemble. Robustness is not a probability of success.

optimizer.objective: Objective: maximise the weighted value of completed tasks, minus total completion time, with a small bonus for keeping human assignments.
optimizer.value: Value = Σ weight × component (life safety, critical infrastructure, economic loss), each normalised 0–100 across candidate tasks. Weights are set by a human.
optimizer.verification: Every solution is re-simulated on the time-dependent road graph; infeasible legs are corrected or forbidden and the model is solved again.
optimizer.modes: Alternatives: policy optimum; robust (rewards slack, 20-min margin); minimal change to the human plan.
optimizer.solver: Solver: Google OR-Tools CP-SAT (routing circuits per crew, vehicle no-overlap, pump and equipment capacity, human constraints).

methodology.bottleneck: Criticality combines newly isolated population, facility criticality and single points of failure when the bottleneck is removed from the road graph at the selected time. Structural candidates come from edge betweenness and cut edges of the network — they are candidates for review, not predictions.

guide.title: User guide
guide.subtitle: Everything you need to work with ARGUS FloodOps — in plain words, step by step.

toc.honesty: What ARGUS does and does not claim

start.intro: ARGUS shows how a flood develops through the real city, which roads, buildings and facilities are affected and when access disappears — and checks whether your response plan still works in time. People decide; ARGUS calculates.
steps: Sign in with your account (demo: planner / argus2026). The interface opens in Kazakh — switch the language at any time with ҚАЗ | РУС | ENG in the top right corner.
On Regional overview choose an area: Atbasar — Zhabai (the real April 2024 flood) or Kokshetau — Kylshakty (training exercise). The card shows status, the plan and the next critical decision.
In Situation room press ▶ on the timeline at the bottom to watch the flood develop. Switch 2D / 3D in the top left corner of the map.
Open Plan to see whether the response plan still works, why it does not, and which alternatives are better.
Nothing changes by itself: ARGUS proposes, a person reviews and approves.

modes.intro: Every number in ARGUS carries a badge that says where it comes from. Look at the badge before you trust a number.

items.LIVE: Live data from a connected provider. Shown only when data really arrived recently.
items.HISTORICAL: Historical replay: the real April 2024 flood in Atbasar on an exercise clock. Real observations and reconstructions — not today's situation.
items.SIMULATION: Exercise data: the Kokshetau flood scenario, plans, resources and injects. For training — not measurements.
items.CACHED: Saved copy of earlier data. If the internet or a provider is down, ARGUS keeps working on saved data and shows how old they are (STALE / OFFLINE).
items.NOT_CONFIGURED: The source is planned but no official connection was provided (Kazhydromet, Tasqyn). ARGUS never invents these data.
items.VISUALIZATION: Smooth playback between frames, the water effect and 3D building heights help reading the map — they add no new prediction.

items: Zoom with the mouse wheel and drag to move. Hold the right mouse button (or Ctrl) and drag to rotate and tilt.
2D / 3D in the top left: 3D raises the terrain and buildings. Building heights are OSM floors × 3 m — an illustration, not a survey.
Camera buttons: ⌂ back to the start view, ⤢ show the whole area, ↻ rotate by 90°.
Layers: switch the flood, buildings, roads, labels, facilities, task sites and the base map on or off.
Click any road, building, bridge or facility to see what it is, its state at the selected time and where the data come from.
Colours: grey road — open, orange — restricted, red dashed — closed. Yellow-to-red buildings are flooded; the darker the blue, the deeper the water.
An object without a name in OpenStreetMap gets a factual label such as "School · #F003". ARGUS never makes up names of real places.
The bar at the bottom is time. Left of NOW is what already happened (analysis), right of NOW is the forecast.
▶ plays the flood; choose the speed 0.5×–4×. ⏮ jumps to the start, ‹ › step frame by frame, "Go to NOW" returns to the current moment.
Drag along the bar or use the ← → keys. Space starts and pauses playback.
Red triangles mark road closures, orange marks are the latest safe departure times of plan tasks.
"+30 min" moves the exercise clock forward (planners only). It is recorded in the audit trail.

overview.what: Both areas at a glance: status, water level, plan and the next critical decision.
overview.how: Click an area card to open its operational map.

situation.what: The operational map: scenario, hydrograph, 2024 history, live context and data freshness.
situation.how: Play the timeline, switch 2D / 3D, click objects. Change the scenario member (LOW / BASE / HIGH) in "Member selection".

impact.what: What is affected at the selected time: buildings, people in flood zones, critical facilities, closed roads.
impact.how: Move the timeline to the peak. Money is not shown unless an approved valuation table exists — exposure is shown as floor area.

windows.what: How much time is left: the latest safe moment to start each task, road closures and sector isolation.
windows.how: Watch "Next critical decision". Red means the window is closing — act before it.

bottlenecks.what: What follows if a bridge, culvert or low road becomes unavailable.
bottlenecks.how: Click a card: you see which sectors, facilities and plan tasks lose access and which detour roads take the load.

plan.what: Will our plan work? Status, WHY chain, stress test and alternatives.
plan.how: Read the red WHY chain, press STRESS TEST PLAN, then GENERATE ALTERNATIVES and compare.

operations.what: Running the approved plan: task board, events, recompute and approvals.
operations.how: Report a road closure or a pump failure, then press RECOMPUTE to get a new draft for approval.

validation.what: How well the model matches the satellite observation of the 2024 flood.
validation.how: Press "Run validation": ARGUS computes IoU, precision, recall and F1 from the masks.

report.what: A printable briefing for decision makers in Kazakh, Russian or English.
report.how: Choose the report language and press "Print / save PDF".

data.what: All inputs: observations, conflicts, resources, road events, facilities, imports and data sources.
data.how: Add or import data here. Every entry records who, when and from which source.

audit.what: Why did the result change? Every change with who, what and when.
audit.how: Choose the area and tick "Only changes that affect results".

admin.what: Providers, outage simulation, users and model versions (administrators).
admin.how: Use "Simulate external provider outage" to show that ARGUS keeps working without external data.

checkPlan.title: Check whether the plan still works
steps: Open Plan.
Look at the status: PLAN VALID or PLAN AT RISK.
Press WHY? to read the chain of causes: scenario → road → resource → task.
The table lists every task: departure, arrival, when the window closes and the time reserve.

stress.title: Stress-test the plan
steps: On Plan press STRESS TEST PLAN.
ARGUS re-runs the plan under many disturbances: higher water, delays, closures, failures.
Robustness shows in how many of them the plan still works. Click a row to see why it fails.

alternatives.title: Find better alternatives
steps: Press GENERATE ALTERNATIVES (CP-SAT optimizer).
Choose the policy and weights — this is your decision, not the computer's.
Compare the alternatives and open a task to read WHY THIS TASK / RESOURCE / NOW.
Nothing is applied automatically: save it as a new version and send it for approval.

approve.title: Approve a plan version (commander)
steps: Open Operations → "Versions awaiting decision".
Mark reviewed → Approve → Activate.
Only the commander can approve. The approved plan is never replaced silently.

roadClosure.title: Report a closed road
steps: Operations → "Report event" → Road closed.
Choose the road, add a note and press Report.
ARGUS recalculates access and the plan. Press RECOMPUTE for a new draft.

scenario.title: Escalate the scenario (exercise)
steps: Situation room → "Member selection": choose HIGH and write the reason.
Or use the one-click BASE → HIGH escalation on the Plan screen.
Each change creates a new scenario version and an audit entry.

language.title: Change the language
steps: Click ҚАЗ, РУС or ENG in the top right corner.
The whole interface switches at once. The report language is chosen separately on the Report screen.

offline.title: Work without internet
steps: ARGUS keeps working on installed and saved data.
Badges show CACHED / STALE / OFFLINE and the age of the data.
An administrator can simulate an outage in Administration to demonstrate it.

addData.intro: Everything you enter is stored with your name, the time and the source, and appears in the audit trail.

observation.title: Water level observation
steps: Data & input → Observations.
Choose the station, enter the level in cm, the source and its type (field, hydropost, forecast, satellite).
Press ADD OBSERVATION. Verified field data outrank hydroposts, which outrank forecasts and models.
If two sources disagree, ARGUS marks a DATA CONFLICT — the commander decides which one counts.

resource.title: Crews, vehicles and pumps
steps: Data & input → Resources: add or update a resource (ID, type, capacity, base).
To test fewer resources, change "Available pumps" on the Plan screen and see the effect immediately.

roadEvent.title: Road event
steps: Data & input → Road events: choose the road, the state (closed or restricted) and the time it applies from.
Press Clear when the road reopens.

facility.title: Critical facility
steps: Data & input → Critical facilities: type, name, longitude and latitude, criticality 0–100.
Coordinates can be copied from any online map.

import.title: Import a file
steps: Data & input → Imports: choose what you import (resources, facilities, observations or road events).
Download the template, fill it in and upload a CSV, XLSX, JSON or GeoJSON file.
Check the preview: invalid rows are listed and never imported silently.
Press CONFIRM IMPORT.

realdata.title: Map and city data
steps: Roads, buildings, population and satellite layers come from the installed real-data packs (command: python -m app.cli install-realdata).
They are downloaded once, checked by checksum and reused on every start — no internet needed afterwards.

roles.intro: What you can do depends on your role. Demo accounts use the password argus2026.

items: Flood surfaces are precomputed scenario members (a terrain-based model calibrated on the 2024 observations) — not a hydrodynamic simulation inside ARGUS.
The Atbasar validation is a historical same-event spatial holdout: it is not the accuracy of future forecasts.
Kokshetau is an uncalibrated training exercise; its impact estimate is conservative and must not be read as a forecast.
Plans, resources and injects are SIMULATION — they are not real DChS/MChS inventories.
3D building heights, smooth playback and the water effect are visualization.
ARGUS never approves or activates anything by itself.
Space — play / pause the timeline
← → — previous / next frame
Home / End — start / end of the timeline
Tab — move between controls; every map object is reachable from the keyboard

items.q: The map is empty or grey
items.a: Right after the server starts, data are prepared once — wait a few seconds. If it stays empty, check that the server is running and press ⌂ (reset view).

items.q: Why is a name in Russian when I chose English?
items.a: Names of real places come from OpenStreetMap as written locally. ARGUS translates the interface, not proper names.

items.q: Why does it say PLAN AT RISK?
items.a: Press WHY? on the Plan screen: it shows the chain of causes — usually a road that closes earlier and a team that loses access.
Every change is in the Audit trail. An administrator can reset the demo in Administration.

items.q: Where is the street base map?
items.a: The OpenStreetMap base map needs internet — switch it on in Layers. Without internet ARGUS shows the terrain and its own data.

welcome.title: Welcome to ARGUS FloodOps
welcome.body: ARGUS shows how a flood develops through the real city and checks whether your response plan still works in time.
steps: Pick an area on this overview
Press ▶ on the timeline to watch the flood
Open Plan to test the response plan
